title: Dialog with a never-laid-out autowrapped Label requests a native window too large and crashes the editor via the graphics driver
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable (Arch package https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/5b4e0cb0fd279832bbdd69fed5354d4e5ad26f88), v4.6.stable (official https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/89cea143987d564363e15d207438530651d943ac), v4.4.stable (official https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/4c311cbee68c0b66ff8ebb8b0defdd9979dd2a41)
- Not tested earlier, but the same zero-width-wrap trigger is reported against 3.2 in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/47005 (still open), so this appears to be a long-standing bug, not a regression. The claimed height varies only with default font metrics which changed in 4.6 with the theme updates (19,254 px in 4.6/4.7; 23,258 px in 4.4).

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable (5b4e0cb) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 18 Jul 2026 17:30:57 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (radeonsi, gfx1201, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.1.4-arch1-1) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.37 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/121591 **rewritten by hand** because of [Godot's contribution policies](https://godotengine.org/article/contribution-policy-2026/). **Note that much more detailed information can be found on the original issue, which I also manually verified to be accurate**, but [I have completely rewritten the report below by hand to comply with Godot's contribution policies and the maintainers request despite my original issue clearly stating that I had already independently verified and reviewed everything](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/121591#issuecomment-5032024578).

**AI Disclosure:** This bug was **initially identified** while using Agentic AI systems, however, **I have independently verified all work, and have completely rewritten all of its output and this entire report myself**, besides the MRP that I have also independently confirmed to demonstrate the bug/crash, which needed no changes, in order to comply with Godot's contribution policies.

If this valid bug is closed again for contribution policy reasons, please be thorough in why this action was taken beyond linking to the original blog post, as I believe this bug report to be legitimate. To show that I am serious about addressing this bug in both Godot and Mesa, [here's the bug report I filed for the other half of this bug with Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/work_items/15913), as the crash is two-sided. Godot should not be sending a window so large that it crashes the graphics driver, and the graphics driver shouldn't allow such a large window to crash the driver. 

> [!WARNING]
> **Note for testers:** reproducing this creates a native window ~19,000+ pixels tall. On Mesa radeonsi + Wayland systems this may crash your process via the graphics driver. If it doesn't, try making a window even taller and it probably will. You might briefly disrupt your compositor. Don't test with saved work, but you weren't going to do that anyways were you?

## What Happens
`AcceptDialog` containing an autowrapped `Label` that has never been through a layout pass opens on its first `popup_centered()`, as a native window sized to the label's **pre-layout minimum**. If the label has a text length of 0, this height gets insanely large, in the 19k pixels tall range, which is so tall that it crashes the graphics driver.

Godot should be clamping the max size of windows to a sensible value to prevent the crash, or the hazard and potential crash should be noted in the documentation, at the very least. Mesa also shouldn't let such a large window bring down the driver, but Godot shouldn't be creating a situation that causes the driver to struggle in the first place.

**Expected:** a dialog never asks the display server for a window taller than the screen (or at minimum, taller than the GPU can present). Windows could be clamped to a sensible maximum value, or at minimum the hazard can be documented.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project and press Run (or `godot --path .`).
2. Read the console: the first popup prints a dialog size and native window size of ~716×19,254 on a 1080p screen; the second popup of the same dialog prints sane. No interaction is needed; the project quits itself.

[godot-window-size-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30226799/godot-window-size-mrp.zip)
